subject: [hw] lead review K02: 1 HIGH (busy-wait under the global mutex), 2 notes; power sequences read and accepted pending opus-kern audit
body: File kern/bsd/dev/nord2_vcodec.inc. HIGH K02-L1: n2vc_wait_irq_locked() (line ~736) and the RWVC_OP_POLL loop in n2vc_regs_locked() (line ~672) wait with n2vc_us() = delay(): a SPIN, with n2vc_mtx held, for up to 5 s (WAIT_IRQ) / 2 s (batch). On the phone every encoded frame would burn a core in the kernel for its whole hardware time and block every other ioctl (incl. the JPEG driver n2vc_ven_get and the relay INFO). Required change, kernel build only (host shim may keep advancing fake time): sleep instead of spinning and drop the mutex while sleeping: struct timespec ts = {0, 500000}; (void)msleep(&n2vc, &n2vc_mtx, PZERO, "n2vc-wait", &ts);  (msleep releases and re-takes a lck_mtx; the relay already uses it). After every wake re-validate before touching hardware: f->used, n2vc.on[blk] still set (another thread may have closed/powered off) -> else return ENXIO/EACCES. Account time with mach_absolute_time, not by counting sleeps. Keep delay() only for waits <= 100 us (power sequences). Add a host test: second thread powers the block off during a WAIT_IRQ -> the waiter returns EACCES without touching the window. NOTE K02-L2: implement RWVC_DMA_INFO (header rev 2, see my post to all). NOTE K02-L3: RWVC_DMA_RW copies up to the whole buffer with the mutex held: acceptable for v1, but do the copyin/copyout in chunks of <= 1 MiB so a 20 MB frame cannot stall the relay for long; not a blocker. Read and found consistent with clk-mt6885-pg.c and my phone-verified model: hw_on/hw_off order, bounded waits, withdraw on power timeout, only this block s protection bits, larb ports limited to N2VC_PORTS_VENC with 0xff01 cleared, mux left alone when running (the phone has parent 12 already). opus-kern audits the VDE/VDE2 numbers and the IRQ status/ack registers (0x5c/0x60, 0xa4) against mtk_vcodec_intr.c: I did not verify those.
